scenes.narration: An Arctic tern can fly up to about 70,000 kilometers in a single year, nearly twice around the Earth.

visual.prompt: a small white Arctic tern with a black cap flying over icy blue water, sharp detail

scenes.narration: It travels from the Arctic to Antarctica and back, chasing endless summer daylight.

visual.prompt: a bright polar sea with floating ice under a low summer sun, wide shot

scenes.narration: Its rival is the bar-tailed godwit, which holds the record for the longest known non-stop flight by a bird.

visual.prompt: a bar-tailed godwit with a long bill standing on a muddy shore at dawn, close shot

scenes.narration: In 2022, a young godwit was tracked flying more than 13,000 kilometers from Alaska to Tasmania in about 11 days without landing.

visual.prompt: a lone shorebird flying over a vast dark ocean at dusk, wide aerial view

scenes.narration: The tern wins on total distance. The godwit wins on a single push without rest.

visual.prompt: two birds flying side by side across an orange sky, silhouette, wide shot

scenes.narration: Scores: yearly distance, tern 10, godwit 8. Non-stop endurance, tern 6, godwit 10.

scenes.narration: While flying, the godwit lives on stored body fat and reportedly even shrinks some of its organs. Which one is the greater traveler?
